session.opened: Your account was signed in to
session.closed: {count, plural, one {A session was signed out} other {# sessions were signed out}}
session.awaitingApproval: A new sign-in is waiting for your approval

reasons.client: It was used from a different browser and system than the one it was opened in.
reasons.address: It was used from a different network address than the one it was opened at.

breach.advice: Everything above is what the address and the browser said about themselves. Change your password if you did not recognise any of it.
breach.title: A session of yours was used by somebody else

test.gone: That destination is switched off or no longer exists.
test.title: Polaris test alert
test.body: If you are reading this, alerts sent here will arrive.

security.account_password_recovered: Your password was replaced from the recovery questions
security.account_recovery_completed: Your password was reset after a recovery request
security.account_pin_set: A quick unlock PIN was set
security.account_pin_cleared: The quick unlock PIN was removed
security.account_phone_set: A phone number was added to your account
security.account_2fa_backup_codes_issued: A new set of backup codes was issued
security.account_passkey_removed: A passkey was removed from your account
security.account_passkey_added: A passkey was added to your account
security.account_login_approval_enabled: Sign-ins now have to be approved
security.account_login_approval_disabled: Sign-ins no longer have to be approved
security.account_new_device_grace_updated: The wait for a new device changed
security.account_session_binding_updated: What your sessions are tied to changed
security.account_session_pinned: A session was tied to its address
security.account_extension_pinned: A browser extension was tied to its address
security.connection_signin_allowed: A connected account may now sign you in
security.connection_signin_refused: A connected account may no longer sign you in
security.account_access_group_created: An address group was added to your sign-in rules
security.account_access_group_updated: An address group in your sign-in rules changed
security.account_access_group_deleted: An address group was removed from your sign-in rules
security.account_email_added: An email address was added to your account
security.account_email_removed: An email address was removed from your account
security.account_ai_key_added: An AI provider key was added
security.account_ai_key_deleted: An AI provider key was removed
security.advice: If this was not you, change your password and sign out every other device.

friends.askedBody: Answer it on your friends page.
friends.acceptedBody: You can now see whatever they show their friends.

domains.downOneBody: {detail}. The service itself may still be running - check the domain's route and the port it points at.
domains.downManyBody: {names}. They went down together, so this is usually the connection or the edge rather than the services themselves.

account.lockedDownBody: Nothing about how it is protected can be changed and no new sign-in works. The devices already signed in keep working, and an administrator has been told.
account.deletingBody: Nothing is removed for {days} days. Sign in before then and it is called off - there is nothing else to do and nobody to ask.
account.disabledTitle: Your account has been switched off
account.disabledBody: Sign in again whenever you like and it comes straight back.
account.notDeletingTitle: Your account will not be deleted
account.backBody: Signing in brought it back. Nothing was lost.
account.recoveryTitle: Someone is locked out of their account
account.recoveryVerified: They answered their recovery questions. Approve it in People to let them set a new password.
account.recoveryUnverified: They could not answer any recovery questions. Check who they are before approving it in People.

safety.lockedDownTitle: An account has been locked down
safety.lockedDownNoDetail: They gave no detail. The account is shut to every change and to new sign-ins until it is lifted.
safety.settledTitle: An administrator has looked at your locked-down account
safety.settledBody: They have finished looking. Lifting the lockdown is still yours to do, under Security.
safety.subject: {name} ({email})

orgs.invitedBody: Accept it to join, or turn it down. Nothing happens until you do.
orgs.couldNotJoinTitle: Somebody you invited to {org} made an account but could not join

scan.blocked: The upload was blocked and removed.
scan.kept: It was kept - review it before opening.
scan.flagged: "{file}" uploaded to "{dropPoint}" was flagged by VirusTotal ({engines, plural, one {# engine} other {# engines}}). {tail}
scan.clean: "{file}" uploaded to "{dropPoint}" passed the VirusTotal scan.
scan.partialTitle: Upload could not be fully scanned
scan.notScanned: "{file}" uploaded to "{dropPoint}" could not be scanned ({detail}). It was kept.

connections.expiredToken: The token you pasted has run out or been withdrawn. Until it is replaced, deploys from your private repositories will be refused.
connections.expiredLink: GitHub no longer accepts that link. Until it is connected again, deploys from your private repositories will be refused.
connections.scopesTitle: Connect {name} again to finish setting it up
connections.scopesBody: Polaris now asks {name} for {asked}, which your account {label} was not linked with. Nothing you have has stopped working - connecting it again is what grants the new part.
connections.deploysHiddenTitle: Your deploys are not showing on {repo}
connections.deploysHiddenToken: GitHub refused to put the deploy on the commit: the token for {label} does not carry Deployments: Read and write on that repository. Everything else about the deploy worked. Replace the token with one that has it, and the next deploy appears on the commit the way Vercel's and Railway's do.
connections.deploysHiddenAccount: GitHub refused to put the deploy on the commit: the account {label} cannot write deployments on that repository. Everything else about the deploy worked. Installing the GitHub App on it, or connecting an account that may, is what puts the deploy on the commit.
connections.suggestBody: You signed up with a {name} address. Linking it confirms the address, and lets you sign in without a password.
connections.refusedBody: Somebody tried to connect their {name} account and it was refused. {name} said: {reason}

modelKeys.expiringTitle: {whose, select, mine {Your} other {The deployment''s}} {provider} key "{name}" expires soon
modelKeys.expiredTitle: {whose, select, mine {Your} other {The deployment''s}} {provider} key "{name}" expired
modelKeys.expiringBody: {count} day(s) left. Replace the key here and runs keep working; leave it and they stop on the day.
modelKeys.expiredMine: It is no longer used. Runs fall back to the next key in your list, or to the deployment's.
modelKeys.expiredDeployment: It is no longer used. Runs fall back to the next key in the list, or to whatever each account brought itself.

update.readyTitle: A Polaris update is ready to install
update.planDaily: It installs itself at {at}, or install it now from Settings.
update.planManual: Install it from Settings, where you can also see what changed.
update.installingBody: Build {sha}. The dashboard keeps serving while the new build starts; Settings shows the log.
update.notStartedTitle: Polaris could not install an update
update.notStartedBody: {reason} Build {sha} is waiting; Settings > Updates installs it once it can.
update.reasonUnavailable: This installation cannot update itself: it updates only by installing it again.
update.reasonDisabled: Updates were switched off for this machine when it was set up.
update.reasonUnreachable: The part of Polaris that installs updates did not answer.
update.failedTitle: A Polaris update failed to install
update.failedBody: Build {sha}. The updater stopped with exit code {code}; Settings has the log and can report it.

address.tunnelGoneBody: {url} stopped answering and its tunnel is no longer running, so it has been dropped from this deployment''s addresses. Share links move to the next address. Settings can raise a new tunnel.
address.offlineBody: Nothing answered at {url}, and neither did anything else - the public resolvers Polaris checks are silent too, so this is the line rather than the address. Nothing about {host} needs changing: it will be reachable again when the connection is. Anything Polaris does outside this network is paused until then.
address.downBody: Nothing answered at {url}. Polaris can reach the internet, so this is about that address rather than about the connection. It is still listed in Settings, marked unreachable.
address.downBodyDetail: Nothing answered at {url} ({detail}). Polaris can reach the internet, so this is about that address rather than about the connection. It is still listed in Settings, marked unreachable.

leftover.title: {count, plural, one {Polaris removed a leftover volume ({size})} other {Polaris removed # leftover volumes ({size})}}

github.appMissingTitle: The GitHub App is missing a permission only you can add
github.appMissingBody: It does not ask for {permissions} yet, so nobody can grant it - there is no request to accept. {where} Each account it is installed on then gets a request to accept. Until then, runner pools and agent runs are refused.
github.setOnApp: Set it on the App''s own permissions page on GitHub and save.
github.waitingTitle: GitHub is waiting for you to accept a permission
github.waitingBody: {logins} has not granted {permissions}. {open} press Review request, then Accept new permissions. Until then, runner pools and agent runs on it are refused. Only the account owner can accept it, so this is one Polaris cannot do for you.
github.openInstallation: Open the installation on GitHub and

deployTest.title: Polaris test event
deployTest.body: This is what a deploy notification from this project will look like.

domainAddress.changedBody: This server's public address changed from {from} to {to}, so {count} DNS {count, plural, one {record was} other {records were}} repointed. Nothing else was touched.
domainAddress.setBody: This server's public address is {to}, so {count} DNS {count, plural, one {record was} other {records were}} repointed.
domainAddress.staleTitle: {domain} does not point at this server
domainAddress.notUpdated: This server now answers on {current}, but the records could not be updated: {detail}
domainAddress.conflict: This server now answers on {current}, but {names} points at {contents}. Polaris does not repoint a record it did not write - change it yourself if it should name this server.

preview.noSecretsTitle: The preview of {pull} has no secrets
preview.noSecretsBody: Secrets are not copied into pull request previews, so it starts without {keys}. Set any it needs on the preview.

disk.freedBody: Polaris handed back everything nothing was using. What is left is volumes and the files somebody put in them, and only a person can decide what goes.
disk.nothingFreedBody: There was nothing left to hand back. What is using it is volumes and the files somebody put in them, and only a person can decide what goes.

router.forward: Forward ports 80 and 443 on your router to this server.
router.port80: Port 80 is needed even for an HTTPS-only site: the certificate is issued over it.
router.certTitle: Reachable, but browsers will warn about the certificate
router.certDetail: {hostname} reaches this server. HTTPS is being served with Polaris''s own certificate rather than one issued for this name, so browsers will not trust it.
router.certWait: A certificate is requested the first time the name is served; check again in a minute.
router.certContact: If it does not arrive, check Certificate contact on the Domains page: it says whether the edge is ready to ask for one, and restarts it when it needs to.
router.answers: It answers{hasStatus, select, yes { {status}} other {}}{hasServer, select, yes {, and calls itself "{server}".} other {.}}
router.routerTitle: Your router is answering instead of Polaris
router.routerCgnat: {hostname} reaches your line, but the reply comes from the router.{answers} Your provider shares one address between its customers, so no forward can bring the request any further than this.
router.routerHome: {hostname} reaches your line, but the reply comes from the router.{answers} Ports 80 and 443 are not reaching this server, so the router answers on its own behalf - which is the error you get in a browser.
router.remoteManagement: If the router still answers once the rules are saved, it is keeping 80 and 443 for its own admin page: turn off remote (WAN) management, or move it to another port.
router.otherTitle: Something else is answering on this domain
router.otherDetail: {hostname} reaches the server, but the reply does not come from Polaris.{answers}
router.findHolder: Find what is holding ports 80 and 443 on this server and stop it, or move it to another port.
router.checkPointing: Check that the domain points at this server and not at another host.
router.cgnatTitle: Your line cannot receive incoming connections
router.cgnatDetail: Nothing answered on {hostname}. Your provider puts you behind carrier-grade NAT, so no port forward can work - the address is shared and it is not yours to open.
router.useTunnel: Use a tunnel to publish the site, which needs no open port.
router.askProvider: Or ask your provider for a public IP address, which some offer on request.
router.silentTitle: Ports 80 and 443 may not reach this server
router.silentHome: Nothing answered on {hostname} from here. Plenty of routers will not route their own public address back inward, so this is not proof on its own - check it from outside the network, on mobile data, to be sure.
router.allowInbound: Allow inbound 80 and 443 in your provider''s firewall or security group.
